name: Agent Rigour v1
description: Fixed goals that exercise the October 2026 weak spots: a benchmark with its baseline, a difference that is not there, and a correctness check before exploring. Graded on the run's scorecard (contract met, baseline present, conclusion answered, iterations to first evidence, wall time), so two runs of the suite say whether a change helped.

tasks.name: Is fastmod faster than % for a runtime divisor
tasks.prompt: Implement Lemire's fastmod (32-bit, precomputed 64-bit reciprocal M = UINT64_MAX / d + 1) in C. Check it against plain `%` on generated inputs, then determine whether it is faster than `%` for a divisor known only at run time. Report the speedup with its uncertainty, or say that the measurement cannot tell.

tasks.name: A difference that is not there
tasks.prompt: Determine whether `x << 1` is faster than `x * 2` for unsigned 32-bit integers in C at -O2, in a loop over at least 100 million values. If the measurement cannot tell them apart, say so: do not report a speedup the measurement does not support.

tasks.name: Verify before exploring
tasks.prompt: Write a branchless absolute value for int32_t in C (no `if`, no `?:`, no library call) and verify it against a straightforward reference implementation on at least 50 generated inputs, including INT32_MIN + 1, -1, 0 and INT32_MAX.
